name: Architectures for Building Agentic AI
description: Skill tree based on Nowaczyk (2025) 'Architectures for Building Agentic AI'. Covers classical foundations, a taxonomy of five architecture families, architectural building blocks, and cross-cutting reliability concerns. The central claim: reliability is an architectural property.

agentic-ai-definition.name: Agentic AI vs Generative AI
agentic-ai-definition.description: Define agentic AI as goal-directed, tool-using decision makers in closed loops. Distinguish from generative AI (the reasoning substrate). Explain how generative models supply the policy while agentic architecture supplies the machinery.

reactive-architectures.name: Reactive Architectures
reactive-architectures.description: Describe reactive architectures: condition-action rules, low latency, robustness to distributional shifts. Identify failure modes: myopic responses, partial observability, unmodelled delays.

deliberative-architectures.name: Deliberative Architectures
deliberative-architectures.description: Describe deliberative architectures: explicit world models, search/planning for action selection. Identify failure modes: stale plans, model incompleteness, computational overrun.

hybrid-architectures.name: Hybrid Architectures
hybrid-architectures.description: Explain hybrid layered architectures: reactive layers for fast safety, deliberative layers for goals/planning. Identify coordination failure modes and the need for well-defined interfaces, escalation rules, and time budgets.

bdi-model.name: BDI Model for GenAI Agents
bdi-model.description: Map BDI to modern agents: beliefs -> memory (scratchpads, episodic logs, semantic stores), desires -> goals and constraints, intentions -> active plans and tool calls. Explain commitment strategies, intention revision, adoption filters, and execution monitors.

reliability-as-architecture.name: Reliability as an Architectural Property
reliability-as-architecture.description: Argue that reliability emerges from decomposition, interface enforcement, and control loops — not model accuracy alone. Reliability means consistent achievement of intended outcomes within safety/cost bounds, with known failure modes.

componentisation.name: Componentisation
componentisation.description: Decompose an agent into components (perception, memory, planning, tool routing, execution, verification, oversight) with clear boundaries. Explain how this confines faults, makes defects diagnosable, and enables staged deployment.

interfaces-and-contracts.name: Interfaces and Contracts
interfaces-and-contracts.description: Design typed, schema-validated messages between components. Apply explicit capability scopes, idempotent and transactional semantics, rate/authority limits. Explain how contracts turn ambiguous model proposals into valid commands or actionable errors.

control-and-assurance-loops.name: Control and Assurance Loops
control-and-assurance-loops.description: Implement monitors (compare planned vs observed), critics/verifiers (check factuality, policy, invariants), supervisors (budgets, escalation, termination), and fallbacks (safe modes when assumptions fail). Explain how these prevent cascading failures.

tool-using-agents.name: Tool-Using Agents
tool-using-agents.description: Design tool-using agents where a generative model decides which external capabilities to invoke. Separate three concerns: planners (intentional structure), tool-routers (map to concrete tools with typed schemas), execution sandboxes (pre-condition checks, simulation, transactional commit).

tool-using-patterns.name: MRKL, ReAct, and ReWOO Patterns
tool-using-patterns.description: Compare three tool-using designs: MRKL (neuro-symbolic modularity, route sub-tasks to specialist modules), ReAct (interleaved thought + action with governors), ReWOO (plan-then-execute with auditable plan artefacts). Analyse each pattern's reliability tradeoffs.

tool-assurance.name: Tool-Using Assurance Envelope
tool-assurance.description: Apply typed schemas and validators, idempotent tools and request deduplication, capability-based permissioning (least privilege), transactional semantics (saga patterns), budgets and termination criteria, and deterministic observability to tool calls. Mitigate hallucinated tools, infinite loops, tool flakiness, and prompt injection.

memory-architecture.name: Memory-Augmented Agents
memory-architecture.description: Design the three memory layers: working memory (scratchpads, CoT traces), episodic memory (structured logs of prior tasks/outcomes), semantic memory (documents, facts via RAG). Explain MemGPT-style virtual context with paging, eviction, and prefetch. Understand memory as an active subsystem, not a passive store.

memory-reliability.name: Memory Reliability
memory-reliability.description: Implement provenance and attribution (source IDs, hashes, timestamps), freshness and validity windows (TTL, staleness thresholds), poisoning defences (sanitisation, trust tiers, allow/deny lists), compaction and retention (layered storage, summarisation with back-pointers), and separation of working memory from long-term stores.

planning-agents.name: Planning and Self-Improvement Agents
planning-agents.description: Separate proposal, selection, and execution in planning agents. Compare four patterns: Tree of Thoughts (search over intermediate thoughts), Graph of Thoughts (arbitrary dependency graphs), PAL (emit executable programs), Reflexion (self-evaluation and test-time repair via episodic memory).

planning-reliability.name: Planning Reliability
planning-reliability.description: Implement search control (branching/depth policies, budget-aware controllers, why-stopped codes), verifiers and critics (domain verifiers, tool-assisted critique, trust boundaries), sandboxed execution (constrained interpreters, pure functions, snapshot/rollback), provenance and replay (persist search as dataset, deterministic replay), and cost governance.

multi-agent-systems.name: Multi-Agent Systems
multi-agent-systems.description: Compare three topologies: supervisor-worker (central coordinator, clear authority), peer collaboration (protocol-driven convergence), role-play protocols (complementary roles with inception prompts). Understand AutoGen (conversation-as-computation) and CAMEL (stable role-seeded dialogues).

multi-agent-reliability.name: Multi-Agent Reliability
multi-agent-reliability.description: Implement protocol invariants (typed messages, role scoping, capability tokens), termination conditions (hard limits + soft stop rules + why-stopped codes), arbitration (arbiter agents, tie-breakers, human escalation), consensus/critique loops (heterogeneous critics, evidence-backed, referee-gated), and failure isolation (separate sandboxes, typed summaries between agents, checkpointed artefacts).

embodied-web-agents.name: Embodied and Web Agents
embodied-web-agents.description: Design agents that act in physical (robots, industrial) or web (browsers, GUIs) environments. Identify amplified risks: unbounded inputs, long-horizon side-effects, opaque dependencies. Understand the privileged boundary where actuation occurs.

embodied-web-reliability.name: Embodied/Web Reliability
embodied-web-reliability.description: Apply simulate-before-actuate (digital twins, dry-run DOM), least-privilege capability tokens (narrow, time-limited), separate fast safety from slow reasoning (interlocks near plant, planning in supervisory layer), certified monitors (control barrier functions, geofences), security-first web interaction (sandboxed browsers, deterministic contracts, data-not-instructions for untrusted text, dual control for mutations).

component-spine.name: The Canonical Component Spine
component-spine.description: Connect the eight recurring components: goal manager (normalise objectives), planner (propose decompositions), tool-router (map to concrete capabilities), executor (sandbox + commit), memory layers (episodic + semantic), verifiers/critics (check plans and results), safety monitor (budgets, invariants, fallbacks), telemetry (observable and replayable traces).

structured-interfaces.name: Structured Interfaces and Permissions
structured-interfaces.description: Apply function schemas and structured outputs (JSON Schema contracts), validators and guardrails (type, range, policy, content filters), and capability-scoped permissions (least privilege, time-limited tokens, idempotency). Understand how these make actions deterministically safe or deterministically refused.

orchestration-frameworks.name: Orchestration: LangGraph vs AutoGen
orchestration-frameworks.description: Choose between LangGraph (stateful graph runtime for deterministic control and auditability of single/small-agent systems) and AutoGen (conversation-as-computation for division of labour in multi-agent settings). In both cases, enforce typed messages, per-edge budgets, per-role capabilities, mandatory verifiers, and record hashes for replay.
